sections.h2: Which Montgomery County office handles delinquent property tax?
sections.html:
The Montgomery County Treasurer handles delinquent taxes, from the County Annex Building at 20 Park Street in Fonda (mailing address PO Box 1500, Fonda, NY 12068). The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, and the phone number on the county's contact page is 518-853-8175.

Assessment records sit with a different office. The county's Real Property Tax Department represents the county in real-property transactions and publishes the tax rolls, tax rates and property data that owners and buyers search before a sale. The treasurer's own page promises direct answers about delinquent taxes and county finances.

  • Overdue balance or payoff figure: Treasurer, Fonda.
  • Assessment, tax roll or rate question: Real Property Tax Department.
  • Value dispute: your town or city assessor and its Board of Assessment Review.

sections.h2: What kind of place is Montgomery County, NY?
sections.html:
Montgomery County is a Mohawk Valley county with Fonda as its seat, bordering the Mohawk River and the Erie Canal corridor west of Schenectady and northwest of Albany. The Census Bureau lists about 403 square miles of land and a July 2025 population estimate of 50,046, up 1.0% from the 2020 base.

The county has ten towns: Amsterdam, Canajoharie, Charleston, Florida, Glen, Minden, Mohawk, Palatine, Root and St. Johnsville. The City of Amsterdam sits inside it, along with villages such as Fort Plain, Fultonville, Canajoharie and Palatine Bridge. Under a charter approved by voters in 2012, the county has had an elected county executive and a nine-member legislature since January 2014.

Housing is inexpensive here. The median owner-occupied home was valued at $157,500 for 2020 to 2024, owners occupy 70.4% of homes, median household income is $64,943 and 15.5% of residents are in poverty. At those prices, a few years of back tax, interest and fees can take a big bite out of what a seller nets.

The Census counts 19,603 households at 2.46 people each and 23,243 housing units, with median gross rent of $940 and a mean commute of 24.0 minutes. Only 105 building permits were issued in 2025, so the county has little new construction competing with resale homes. A buyer who accepts the home as it stands removes the repair question from the sale, leaving the tax payoff as the main item to settle.

sections.h2: When are Montgomery County grievance days?
sections.html:
Most Montgomery County towns hold Grievance Day on the fourth Tuesday in May, while the City of Amsterdam holds its own on the third Tuesday in January. The county's Real Property site lists each municipality, and a few towns shift by a few days.

Montgomery County grievance dates, from the county Real Property site
MunicipalityGrievance Day
City of AmsterdamThird Tuesday in January
Town of AmsterdamSecond Monday after the fourth Tuesday in May
CharlestonFirst Wednesday after the fourth Tuesday in May
Glen and St. JohnsvilleFirst Thursday after the fourth Tuesday in May
Canajoharie, Florida, Minden, Mohawk, Palatine, RootFourth Tuesday in May

Source: Montgomery County grievance dates. In 2027 that puts the City of Amsterdam on January 19 and the fourth-Tuesday towns on May 25.

sections.h2: How does the City of Amsterdam calendar differ from the towns?
sections.html:
The City of Amsterdam assesses on a winter schedule that runs ahead of the towns by months. Its valuation date and taxable status date are both December 1, the tentative roll is filed January 1, and the final roll is filed March 1.

The county's page then gives the city's judicial deadlines: a small claims assessment review application and an Article 7 certiorari filing are both due March 31, which is 30 days after the final roll is filed. A homeowner needs to have gone before the Board of Assessment Review first to use small claims. City tax bills and Greater Amsterdam School District bills go out July 1, while county tax bills go out January 1 based on the final roll.

If your home is inside the city, an appeal window that opened in January 2026 is already closed, and the next one is January 2027. Sellers in a town have more time, since the May Grievance Day is still months off.

sections.h2: When does Montgomery County post rolls and rates?
sections.html:
The county's news archive shows a steady yearly pattern for posting assessment and tax data on the Real Property site. Following that pattern lets you know when a value or rate figure is likely to be online.

  • Tentative assessment rolls for the towns appear in early May.
  • Final assessment rolls follow in early July.
  • Village tax rates are posted around June, and City of Amsterdam rates in July.
  • School district tax rates appear in September.
  • Town and county tax rolls and rates, plus the city's tentative roll, appear in early January.

Use these postings to check your parcel before you list. A seller who looks up the roll in May and the rate in January can estimate the next bill with real numbers, rather than guessing from last year's.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Montgomery County home with property tax owed?
sections.html:
Call the Treasurer in Fonda and ask for a payoff figure on your parcel, then compare it with an offer. The county's treasurer page invites questions about delinquent taxes, and the redemption rule in state law gives you a defined period to pay. Under RPTL 1110, a property with a delinquent lien can be redeemed by paying the lien and the charges authorized by law, and the period ends two years after the lien date unless the published notice names a later date.

A sale that pays cash and accepts the house as it stands can close faster than a retail listing, which matters when you want the balance cleared before it grows. In a county where the median home is valued near $157,500, fast action keeps fees from outrunning your equity.

The same logic applies if you plan to contest value before selling. Homeowners in towns can still prepare for May 2027 by pulling the town's tentative roll when it posts in early May, gathering recent sales of similar homes, and getting an appraisal if the figure looks far off. The state notes there is no cost to grieve and no need for a lawyer, and that you can only challenge the assessment on the current tentative roll, not past years.

  1. Request a current payoff from the Treasurer, 518-853-8175.
  2. Check your town's or the city's assessment calendar for any open appeal window.
  3. Pick a closing date with enough time for the balance to be paid from proceeds.

faqs.q: Where is the Montgomery County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is in the County Annex Building at 20 Park Street, Fonda, NY 12068 (PO Box 1500). Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:00 PM, and the phone number is 518-853-8175.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day for a Montgomery County town?
faqs.a: In most towns it is the fourth Tuesday in May, which is May 25, 2027. Charleston, Glen, St. Johnsville and the Town of Amsterdam use dates a few days later, and the City of Amsterdam uses the third Tuesday in January.

faqs.q: Do I have a time limit to redeem a tax lien in Montgomery County?
faqs.a: Yes. RPTL 1110 sets the redemption period at two years after the lien date, unless the published notice gives a later date or a tax district has adopted a different period for certain properties.

faqs.q: When do Montgomery County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: The county's Amsterdam calendar shows county bills on January 1, and city and Greater Amsterdam School District bills on July 1. For a town, ask your tax collector for local installment dates.

faqs.q: How do I contest an assessment after the Board decides?
faqs.a: Homeowners can apply for Small Claims Assessment Review, which New York's tax department lists at a $30 filing fee, or begin an Article 7 proceeding. Either must start within 30 days of the final roll being filed.
